report.verdict: A customer success profile with strong renewal work, hidden behind a job-search headline and a thin About.
write_up: You managed mid-market shipping software accounts after working in support. A recruiter has a reason to message you, though the headline and About make them work to find that reason.

The Parcelwise renewal line is the model: it names the conversations you ran and the share of accounts renewed by revenue. Your account book and onboarding guide give you more to draw on for the About.

Start by putting customer success and shipping software in the headline, then bring the account and renewal work into the About. Give the earlier support job a little more substance too. A recruiter can then see both your customer success work and the support experience behind it.

cards.line: Open to work | Seeking new opportunities in Customer Success
cards.cannot_tell: The headline spends most of its space on your search. You managed mid-market accounts for a shipping software company, and that's the work to put first.
cards.example: Customer Success | Mid-market accounts | Shipping software
cards.question: What kind of customer success work did you spend the most time doing?

cards.line: Customer success professional currently seeking my next opportunity. Open to remote roles. Please reach out if you think I could be a fit for your team.
cards.cannot_tell: This tells a recruiter what you're looking for, but not what you did for customers. Your Parcelwise job has the account and renewal work to open with.
cards.example: I managed a book of 85 mid-market accounts for a shipping software company. I ran quarterly business reviews and renewal conversations, renewing 91% of accounts by revenue in 2025. I also wrote the onboarding guide new accounts get in their first week.
cards.question: What did customers use the onboarding guide to do in their first week?

cards.cannot_tell: This title doesn't tell a stranger that you managed accounts and renewals. Keep the Parcelwise title, and add the standard title that accurately describes your work beside it.
cards.example: Customer Happiness Hero II | [standard title for your work]
cards.question: At another company, would this work be called Customer Success Manager or Account Manager?

cards.where: Parcelwise, Customer Happiness Hero II, description
cards.line: Ran quarterly business reviews and renewal conversations; renewed 91% of accounts by revenue in 2025.
cards.cannot_tell: This is the line to use as a model. It names the work and the renewal figure, so a recruiter doesn't have to guess what you did.
Zendesk names the tool, but the tickets could cover many kinds of customer problems. Add the issues you handled and who contacted you.
cards.example: Answered support tickets in Zendesk for [who contacted you], including [types of issues].
cards.question: What kinds of issues did you handle in Zendesk, and who was sending the tickets?

cards.cannot_tell: Problem Solving is a broad trait. Your quarterly business reviews and renewal conversations name the customer success work more directly.
cards.example: Quarterly business reviews | Renewal conversations | Zendesk
cards.question: Which of those three did you use most often in your Parcelwise work?

fit.why: Your headline names Customer Success, and your Parcelwise job describes managing accounts, renewals and onboarding.
fit.level: mid-level, the Customer Happiness Hero II title and responsibility for a book of 85 mid-market accounts
fit.note: 'Customer Success' is in your headline. 'Mid-market accounts', 'quarterly business reviews' and 'renewal conversations' are in your Parcelwise description. 'Zendesk' is in your top skills and Support Specialist description. Someone hiring for this work may also search for Customer Success Manager, customer health and churn; those terms aren't on your profile. Add them only if they accurately describe your work. Move 'mid-market accounts' into your headline.
